keyword.$description: Code keywords and storage declarations, and markup tags; blue. Operators and punctuation stay neutral.

string.$description: Code strings and quoted values; green. Never used as a success indicator.

constant.$description: Code numbers, booleans and constants; amber. Never used as a warning indicator.

function.$description: Code functions, types and classes; purple.

comment.$description: Code comments; quiet, but still at least 4.5:1 on the code surface. No italic font is required.

accent.$description: Accent classes. A product picks one with data-accent on its root, or none. A class is one ink per theme, painted only as a dot or icon beside ink words, for a product's council-approved role. It is not a custom property of its own: the generated rules put both themes in one light-dark() value on --basalt-accent-ink.

cobalt.$description: Cobalt, hue 264. The one accent class Basalt ships; N1 uses it for "needs you". Never a fill, wash, border, link, focus ring, selection, checked control, status or code colour; syntax-keyword blue is at hue 255.

surface.$description: The page sits below white so white surfaces lift without a shadow; sunken areas step darker.

0.$description: Level 0, the page. A depth is one of four levels; a panel is one level above what it sits on, and level 3 is the cap.

1.$description: Level 1: a panel directly on the page, a popup opened from the page or a sidebar, and the modals' own surface (dialog, sheet, command menu). In light, levels 1 to 3 are all white: nesting shows by the rim (and a shadow when floating), never darker-is-higher.

2.$description: Level 2: a panel in a panel, a popup opened from a card or a modal, the command menu's input band, a modal's inner panels.

3.$description: Level 3: the deepest panel, a popup opened from a level-2 panel, a tooltip, a toast. Nothing nests below it.

page.$description: The page, and app sidebars. The darkest layer in both themes.

raised.$description: Cards, tables, inputs and secondary buttons, on surface-page.

overlay.$description: Level 2: a panel in a panel, and a popup opened from a card or a modal. A menu, select or popover opened from the page or a sidebar is level 1 (surface-raised); a dialog, sheet and the command menu reset to level 1 as well.

top.$description: Tooltips, and the selected pill of a segmented control.

sunken.$description: Wells and code blocks, set into a raised surface.

well-2.$description: A well one level deeper. In light every well is surface-sunken; only dark steps by level.

well-3.$description: A well at level 3. In light every well is surface-sunken; only dark steps by level.

sunken-strong.$description: Table headers and segmented-control tracks: bands, not boxes.

kbd.$description: The fill of a keyboard-key chip. No border. Text on it is text-secondary, or text-primary on a hover or selected wash.

chrome.$description: The smoked fill of a sticky header bar (basalt-chrome): the page, #fafafa, at 92%, over a backdrop blurred by blur-chrome. The only translucent surface in Basalt. Only text-primary and text-secondary may sit on it; never tertiary, never stacked under another translucent layer. Opaque surface-page without backdrop-filter, with reduced transparency, in print. Web only: native bars use the platform bar material or stay opaque.

placeholder.$description: Skeletons and other loading placeholders: visible on the page in both themes.

primary.$description: Body text, headings and labels, on every surface.

secondary.$description: Descriptions, metadata, unselected tabs and icons by default. Also the focus colour.

tertiary.$description: Placeholders, shortcuts and hashes. On a hover or selected wash, use text-secondary instead.

disabled.$description: Disabled controls only (exempt from WCAG contrast); never for readable content.

rim.$description: A panel's rim: a real 1px border, uniform in light. Panels only, never controls or chips.

rim-top.$description: A panel's top edge: the same colour as the rim in light (a top highlight on white would be invisible).

hairline.$description: Decorative 1px lines around secondary buttons, badges and avatars, via shadow-hairline. Panels use the rim.

hover.$description: The hairline of a hovered control: one step brighter, never a colour. Under more contrast it is text-secondary, so a hovered edge is never fainter than the edge at rest.

divider.$description: Rules between table rows, menu groups and card sections.

input.$description: Input boundaries: 3:1 or better on every surface (WCAG 1.4.11).

field.$description: A field's boundary (an input, a select, a number field, a choice box, a switch): the input boundary. Under more contrast it steps to text-secondary (field-contrast), so a field keeps the strongest line.

focus.$description: The 2px focus outline, offset 2px, on every focusable control.

selected.$description: Selected wash: the lit row's plate, the nav pill, a selected table row's band. A wash alone is about 1.2:1, so the state has a second cue: the ink step to primary, a check, a pill or a checked box.

primary.$description: The one primary action per view: the inverse of the page.

primary-hover.$description: action-primary on hover: pure white on dark, pure black on light.

primary-press.$description: action-primary while pressed: 85% of action-primary toward the page colour (about #bfbfbf in dark, #333333 in light). A press is a colour step; Button and IconButton also scale to .98.

danger.$description: Destructive actions and errors: red text, red hairline, a dot. Never a fill.

success.$description: A success or healthy dot, always beside a word.

warning.$description: A warning or in-progress dot, always beside a word.

observed.$description: Every observed series in a chart: lines, markers, bars and the outline of a day that is not yet final.

plan.$description: A chart's plan: the stroke, and the edges of a band. Never a series.

band.$description: A plan band's fill between its two edges. Decorative; the edges carry it.

missing.$description: The hatch that marks missing data in a chart.

baseline.$description: A chart's zero line, drawn only where the scale reaches zero.

axis.$description: A chart's axis labels and the words for a gap.

field.$description: The ground of drawn art and of a stage. It is the page colour, so a stage meets the page with no seam, and it is the stage's placeholder while the art loads.

tone-1.$description: The first step off the field: a sky's horizon, a far ridge, a shadow.

tone-2.$description: Middle forms, and the last tone a quiet zone may hold.

tone-3.$description: Detail starts here: lit edges, lines, most stars. Never in a quiet zone.

mark.$description: The strongest point drawn art may reach. It is text-primary, so art never outshouts the words.

quiet-limit.$description: In a quiet zone no pixel is lighter (dark) or darker (light) than this: the stage's headroom under the bar, and each data-quiet zone. Primary and secondary text and the focus ring hold their contrast on it.

line-contrast.$description: More contrast, lines: a hairline, a divider, a rim and the pill's hairline are drawn in the input boundary's value (border-input), 3:1 or better on every surface. An alias, no new colour. Used only when a person asks for more contrast (prefers-contrast: more; colorSchemeContrast .increased).

ink-contrast.$description: More contrast, ink: tertiary text is drawn as text-secondary. An alias, no new colour.

field-contrast.$description: More contrast, a field's boundary: border-field is drawn as text-secondary, about 7:1 on every surface. An alias, no new colour.

shadow.$description: Controls and small marks keep the hairline (the second ring is the page colour behind it, so the translucent line reads the same on any background). Panels have a rim instead: border-rim.

hairline.$description: Secondary buttons, avatars and the current page: a translucent line backed by the page colour. Panels use the rim, not this.

overlay.$description: Menus, popovers and tooltips. The drop only: the edge is the rim (border-rim), never a ring here.

modal.$description: Dialogs and sheets. The drop only: the edge is the rim (border-rim).
